faqs.answer: If your roof has isolated leaks and is under 15 years old, repair may suffice. Widespread issues or roofs over 20 years typically need replacement.

faqs.question: What causes bricks to crumble (spalling)?
faqs.answer: Spalling is caused by water absorption and freeze-thaw cycles, where trapped water freezes, expands, and fractures the brick's surface.

faqs.answer: Yes, skilled masons can carefully extract and replace individual bricks while preserving adjacent masonry perfectly intact.

faqs.question: What is NYC Local Law 11 (FISP) and does my building require it?

faqs.question: Why is historic lime mortar important instead of modern Portland cement?
faqs.answer: Historic bricks are soft and porous. Using excessively hard Portland cement creates thermal stress that crushes brick faces (spalling). We custom-mix high-calcium lime Type N mortar matching the historic elasticity.

faqs.question: What causes parapet walls to lean or bow outward on NYC brownstones?
faqs.answer: Thermal expansion and freeze-thaw cycles cause the roof-facing masonry to expand faster than the cold street side, creating cumulative eccentric pressure that tilts the wall toward the street.

faqs.question: What causes window lintels to crack the surrounding brickwork?
faqs.answer: When steel lintels over windows rust without protection, rust jacking expands their volume by up to ten times, lifting masonry above into diagonal stair-step cracks. We replace rusted lintels with galvanized or stainless steel units.

faqs.question: What are the early warning signs that a brick building facade needs restoration?
faqs.answer: Visible indicators include crumbling mortar joints, cracked or bulging bricks, rust stains near window headers, and water stains on interior walls. When exterior mortar degrades, driving rain seeps behind the brick veneer, causing hidden steel ties and window lintels to oxidize and expand. This expansion exerts enormous outward pressure that cracks outer masonry courses. If you spot spalling brick faces falling to the street or notice fine stair-step cracks along mortar lines, an exterior restoration is necessary to prevent further structural damage and maintain public safety.

faqs.question: How do you match mortar color and texture on historic buildings?
faqs.answer: We take physical samples of original mortar from protected sections of the wall and blend sand, lime, and pigments to match the original composition. Historic brickwork requires soft, vapor-permeable lime mortars rather than rigid modern Portland cements, which can trap moisture and cause older bricks to fracture. Our team tests sample patches directly on inconspicuous wall sections, allowing them to dry fully before client approval, ensuring the finished repointing seamlessly honors the architectural character of the building and accommodates natural thermal flexibility.

faqs.question: What permits are required before setting up scaffolding for facade work?
faqs.answer: Facade repairs involving scaffolding or sidewalk sheds require permits from the municipal building department and transportation agency. Because sidewalk sheds occupy public walkways and scaffolding alters building access, safety plans and structural load calculations must be filed before erection begins. Mega Contracting NY Group works alongside licensed design professionals to verify all staging filings, ensuring street-level protection sheds and suspended scaffolding comply with municipal pedestrian safety mandates before crews begin masonry restoration on upper stories.

faqs.question: Why do steel window lintels cause cracks in exterior brickwork?
faqs.answer: Unprotected steel lintels rust over time, expanding up to several times their original thickness and lifting the masonry above them. This phenomenon, known in the building trade as rust jacking, creates severe horizontal and stair-step cracks above window and door openings. During facade restoration, we remove loose brick courses above the opening, strip rust from the steel or replace deteriorated lintels with new galvanized units, wrap them in waterproof membrane flashing, and relay the masonry courses with weep tubes to discharge moisture.

faqs.question: How often should a multi-story building facade undergo maintenance?
faqs.answer: Building facades should receive visual inspections annually and comprehensive preventative maintenance every five to ten years depending on weather exposure. High-rise structures and buildings exposed to prevailing winds experience accelerated mortar wear and sealant failure around window perimeters. Proactive maintenance, such as repointing deteriorating joints and resealing expansion joints early, prevents costly emergency repairs and structural stabilization needs later. Regular care preserves structural integrity and keeps your building envelope watertight across changing seasons.

faqs.question: Can facade restoration work proceed during cold winter weather in New York?
faqs.answer: Masonry repointing can proceed during winter months only when proper thermal enclosures and temporary heating equipment protect the curing mortar. Water-based mortar mixes must remain above freezing temperatures during application and throughout their critical curing window to develop proper bonding strength. During cold weather projects, we construct temporary plastic sheeting enclosures around scaffolding platforms and deploy approved heating units to maintain consistent working temperatures that safeguard mortar integrity until chemical hydration finishes completely.

faqs.question: What causes sudden masonry collapse?
faqs.answer: Common causes include water infiltration/freeze-thaw deterioration, foundation settlement, vehicle impact, or deferred maintenance over many decades.

faqs.question: How often should brick facades be repointed (tuckpointed) in NYC?
faqs.answer: High-exposure NYC exterior facades typically require repointing every 25 to 30 years, while exposed rooftop parapets, chimneys, and windward elevations may require service every 15 to 20 years.

faqs.question: What is NYC Local Law 11 (FISP) and does my building require it?
faqs.answer: Local Law 11 mandates that all NYC buildings taller than six stories must have their exterior walls and appurtenances inspected by a Qualified Exterior Wall Inspector (QEWI) every five years.

faqs.question: Why is historic lime mortar important instead of modern Portland cement?
faqs.answer: Historic bricks are soft and porous. Using excessively hard Portland cement creates thermal stress that crushes brick faces (spalling). We custom-mix high-calcium lime Type N mortar matching the historic elasticity.

faqs.question: What causes parapet walls to lean or bow outward on NYC brownstones?
faqs.answer: Thermal expansion and freeze-thaw cycles cause the roof-facing masonry to expand faster than the cold street side, creating cumulative eccentric pressure that tilts the wall toward the street.

faqs.question: What causes window lintels to crack the surrounding brickwork?
faqs.answer: When steel lintels over windows rust without protection, rust jacking expands their volume by up to ten times, lifting masonry above into diagonal stair-step cracks. We replace rusted lintels with galvanized or stainless steel units.

faqs.question: Can sunken or cracked concrete flags be patched instead of completely replaced?
faqs.answer: Complete flag replacement is the standard and durable method because thin surface patches peel away quickly under seasonal freezing. When concrete cracks or sinks due to sub-base erosion, spreading a thin layer of cement over the top does not fix the hollow ground beneath it. Winter moisture enters hairline gaps, freezes, and breaks the patch apart within months. We remove the entire damaged flag down to the soil, rebuild the compacted gravel base, and pour a fresh full-depth slab that withstands winter de-icing materials.

faqs.question: How thick should a residential concrete sidewalk slab be poured?
faqs.answer: Residential sidewalk slabs are typically poured four inches thick over a compacted aggregate base, while driveway crossings require seven inches. The extra depth at driveway intersections provides the load-bearing strength needed to support passenger cars, delivery vans, and light utility vehicles without cracking. In pedestrian-only areas, a four-inch depth provides long-term stability when placed over well-compacted gravel. Our team installs appropriate reinforcement and expansion joint filler between flags to accommodate natural seasonal thermal movement.

faqs.question: How long does it take for new concrete to cure before people can walk on it?

faqs.question: What causes sidewalk concrete to crack, buckle, and become uneven over time?
faqs.answer: Sidewalk damage in New York is primarily caused by freeze-thaw cycles, sub-base soil erosion, and expanding tree roots beneath the slabs. Water penetrates tiny fissures in the concrete during autumn rains, then expands as it freezes during winter drops in temperature, forcing the concrete apart. faqs.question: Can DOB violations affect mortgage approval?

faqs.question: How long does DOB violation removal take?

faqs.question: What are common concrete-related DOB violations?

faqs.question: Do I need an architect for DOB violation removal?

faqs.question: What is a NYC DOT Sidewalk Violation and how do I clear it?
faqs.answer: A DOT violation is issued under NYC Administrative Code §19-152 for trip hazards, cracked flags, or improper slope. To clear it, a licensed contractor must pull street opening permits, replace defective concrete, and submit a formal dismissal request.

faqs.question: How much time do property owners have to repair a DOT sidewalk citation?
faqs.answer: Property owners have 75 days from the notice date to complete repairs. If ignored, the City may dispatch its own contractor to perform the work at premium municipal rates and place a tax lien on the property.

faqs.question: What concrete strength is required by NYC Department of Transportation?
faqs.answer: NYC DOT specifications mandate a minimum compressive strength of 4,000 PSI with 6% air entrainment, poured 4 inches thick for pedestrian walkways and 7 inches thick across active driveways.

faqs.question: Who is responsible for sidewalk damage caused by City street tree roots?
faqs.answer: While adjacent property owners must maintain safe sidewalks, repairs involving City street trees require coordination with the NYC Department of Parks & Recreation for root pruning permits. We handle all agency coordination.

faqs.question: What causes foundation walls to crack and shift in urban residential buildings?
faqs.answer: Foundation damage is primarily driven by soil settlement, excessive hydrostatic pressure from poor surface drainage, and natural seasonal freeze-thaw cycles. When soil beneath a footing dries out during droughts or washes away from leaking water mains, the footing settles unevenly, producing diagonal or stair-step cracks. Conversely, saturated soil expands against exterior basement walls, exerting hydrostatic force that causes concrete blocks or brick foundations to bow inward. We assess these soil pressures before implementing structural repairs that permanently stabilize walls and footing beds.

faqs.question: What is foundation underpinning and when is it required?
faqs.answer: Foundation underpinning is the process of extending existing building footings deeper into the ground to reach stable, load-bearing soil strata. It is required when a building is settling unevenly, when nearby deep excavation threatens foundation stability, or when an owner wishes to lower a basement floor to increase ceiling height. Underpinning is completed by excavating sequential pits beneath the foundation in alternating stages, filling them with reinforced concrete to create a deeper, stable base that prevents structural shifts and settlement.

faqs.question: How do you repair water leaking through basement foundation cracks?
faqs.answer: We repair foundation leaks through high-pressure polyurethane foam injection from the inside or by applying continuous waterproof membranes from the exterior. Polyurethane injection expands rapidly upon contact with moisture, sealing the full thickness of the concrete crack from front to back to block water. For comprehensive protection, excavating the exterior foundation to apply rubberized waterproofing coatings, dimpled drainage boards, and footing drainage pipes provides the most effective long-term defense against groundwater intrusion during heavy rains and rising water tables.

faqs.question: Are horizontal cracks in foundation walls more dangerous than vertical cracks?
faqs.answer: Yes, horizontal cracks are significantly more dangerous because they indicate that outside soil pressure is causing the foundation wall to bow and fail inward. Vertical hairline cracks often result from normal concrete shrinkage during initial curing and can usually be sealed with surface epoxies. Horizontal cracks along mortar joints or mid-height on concrete walls signal structural compromise from hydrostatic force, requiring immediate reinforcement, wall anchors, or steel I-beam bracing to prevent wall collapse. Our technicians install carbon fiber reinforcement straps and heavy-gauge structural steel soldier beams anchored securely to basement floor slabs and overhead framing joists.

faqs.question: Do foundation repairs require engineering plans and municipal building permits?
faqs.answer: Yes, structural foundation repairs, underpinning, and footing modifications require detailed engineering drawings stamped by a licensed professional engineer and approved city permits. Because foundation work alters the primary support structure of a building, municipal authorities strictly regulate excavation depths, shoring procedures, and concrete mix strengths. Mega Contracting NY Group works alongside licensed structural engineers and registered architects to execute permitted repairs in full compliance with municipal building codes and safety regulations, coordinating geotechnical soil borings without unnecessary project delays.

faqs.question: Can a sagging or uneven house floor be leveled by repairing the foundation?
faqs.answer: Yes, interior floors can often be leveled by lifting settled foundation footings with hydraulic jacks or installing adjustable steel support columns in the basement. When foundation walls settle or central wooden girders rot from moisture exposure, floors above sag toward the center of the home. By stabilizing the foundation perimeter and lifting central load-bearing girders back to level, we restore structural stability and eliminate sloping floors throughout your residence, re-establishing proper door and window frame clearances. Our carpentry specialists also shim under-dimensioned joists and install supplemental timber beams to reinforce weak spans across wide residential living spaces.

faqs.question: Do I need a building permit to remodel a residential kitchen in New York?

faqs.question: What is the recommended layout for an efficient residential kitchen?

faqs.question: What electrical upgrades are required for modern kitchen appliances?

Outdated kitchens frequently lack adequate electrical capacity, causing breakers to trip when microwaves, toaster ovens, and coffee makers operate at the same time. Our licensed electrical partners upgrade electrical panels, run new wiring according to current municipal safety standards, and install energy-efficient under-cabinet LED task lighting that illuminates food preparation counters beautifully.

faqs.question: Which countertop material offers the best balance of durability and low maintenance?

Unlike natural marble, which etches easily from lemon juice or vinegar, and granite, which requires annual sealing, quartz withstands heavy everyday culinary use effortlessly. It is available in hundreds of colors and realistic marble patterns, making it an ideal choice for busy residential kitchens seeking long-term performance and aesthetic elegance.

faqs.question: Can a load-bearing wall be removed to create an open-concept kitchen?

faqs.question: Can you convert an old bathtub into a modern walk-in shower?

faqs.question: How do you handle ventilation requirements in bathrooms without windows?

Proper mechanical ventilation prevents condensation from collecting on painted surfaces, inhibits bathroom mold growth, and preserves cabinetry finishes over years of everyday use without disturbing nearby sleeping areas.

faqs.question: What types of flooring tiles are best suited for bathroom floors?

Porcelain is denser and less porous than standard ceramic, making it resistant to moisture, stains, and cracking. We recommend non-slip textured porcelain mosaics or large-format tiles with rectified edges for safety and longevity in humid bathroom environments.

faqs.question: How do I know if stucco needs repair?
faqs.answer: Signs include hairline cracks, bulging areas, hollow sounds when tapped, efflorescence (white stains), or visible water staining.

faqs.answer: Small repairs: 1-2 days. Large sections: 3-7 days depending on access, weather, and curing requirements.

faqs.answer: Yes, using cold-weather additives and protection, though spring through fall offers optimal curing conditions.

faqs.question: What causes stucco to crack?
faqs.answer: Building settlement, temperature fluctuations, freeze-thaw cycles, impact damage, or improper original installation are common causes.

faqs.question: What is the difference between traditional stucco and EIFS synthetic stucco?
faqs.answer: Traditional stucco is a thick (7/8-inch) Portland cement-based composite on metal lath. EIFS (Exterior Insulation and Finish System) incorporates a continuous foam insulation board behind a polymer acrylic finish, offering superior thermal R-values.

faqs.question: Can stucco be applied directly over existing brick or concrete block?
faqs.answer: Yes, structurally sound unpainted brick or cinder block can receive direct stucco bonding with a polymer bonding slurry. Painted or deteriorating surfaces require expanded metal lath mechanically fastened to the masonry.

faqs.question: How do you prevent stucco from cracking during NYC temperature extremes?

faqs.question: What causes stucco to bubble, blister, or peel away from the wall?

faqs.question: How quickly does mold begin to grow after indoor water intrusion occurs?
faqs.answer: Mold spores can begin germinating on wet drywall, wood framing, and carpeting within twenty-four to forty-eight hours of moisture exposure. Because mold thrives in damp, warm, and stagnant environments, fast action to extract standing water and circulate dry air is critical. Delaying extraction allows microbial colonies to establish themselves deep within cellulose materials, dramatically increasing repair costs. Our rapid deployment units respond swiftly to extract moisture and initiate drying before mold colonies can form, protecting indoor air quality and occupants.

faqs.question: What is the difference between clean water, gray water, and black water damage?
faqs.answer: Clean water originates from broken supply pipes and presents no immediate biological hazard, while gray and black water contain harmful contaminants. Gray water comes from washing machine overflows or dishwashers and may carry detergents and bacteria. Black water from sewage backups, river floods, or toilet overflows carries dangerous pathogens, viruses, and organic waste. Gray and black water incidents require specialized containment, complete disposal of porous items, and sanitization before rebuilding can proceed safely.

faqs.question: Can water-damaged hardwood floors and subflooring be saved?
faqs.answer: Hardwood floors and plywood subfloors can often be saved if structural drying equipment is deployed before deep wood cupping and delamination occur. We utilize specialized floor drying mats and high-powered vacuum extraction systems that pull trapped water directly up through the seams of hardwood planks. If water has penetrated beneath the subfloor for multiple days, hardwood may warp permanently, necessitating selective removal and replacement of the damaged section to prevent mold underneath while salvaging adjoining rooms.

faqs.question: Why do technicians make flood cuts on drywall after water damage?
faqs.answer: Technicians make flood cuts twelve to twenty-four inches above the high-water line to remove saturated drywall and wet insulation trapped inside wall cavities. Drywall acts like a sponge, wicking moisture vertically through its gypsum core and paper backing. Removing the bottom portion of the wall opens the wall cavity, allowing high-velocity air to circulate around framing studs and preventing mold colonies from growing on damp insulation inside the walls.

faqs.question: How do you know when structural building materials are completely dry?
faqs.answer: We determine that materials are completely dry by taking daily readings with calibrated moisture meters and comparing them to dry standard benchmarks. Surface touch is never an accurate gauge of dryness because framing timbers can feel dry on the outside while retaining high moisture levels at their core. We monitor and record moisture levels daily until wood studs and masonry dry to acceptable equilibrium moisture levels, ensuring structural safety before closing walls.

faqs.question: Does homeowners or commercial property insurance cover sudden water damage?
faqs.answer: Most standard property insurance policies cover sudden and accidental water damage, such as a burst frozen pipe, but exclude slow, unaddressed leaks. Flood damage caused by outdoor storm surges or street runoff typically requires a dedicated flood insurance policy rather than standard coverage. We provide property owners with detailed moisture logs, photographs, and line-item remediation reports to help document the sudden nature of the event for their insurance carrier during the claims process.

faqs.question: Is board-up service permanent?
faqs.answer: No, board-up provides secure, weatherproof temporary protection until permanent window, door, or roof repairs can be scheduled.

faqs.question: How long does board-up last?
faqs.answer: Professional board-up remains weatherproof for 30-90 days, allowing time for insurance approval and permanent repair scheduling.

faqs.question: Do you match paint or finishes?
faqs.answer: Emergency board-up uses unpainted plywood. Color matching, decorative panels, or security screens cost extra and take 24-48 hours longer.

faqs.question: What about broken glass cleanup?
faqs.answer: Our board-up service includes interior and exterior glass cleanup within accessible areas for immediate safety and security.

faqs.question: Does insurance cover board-up costs?
faqs.answer: Most property insurance policies cover emergency board-up and tarping as part of loss mitigation coverage after covered perils.

faqs.question: How fast can your emergency response team arrive on-site in NYC?
faqs.answer: Our emergency mobilization units are stationed strategically across the five boroughs and arrive on-site within 60 to 120 minutes of your call, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

faqs.question: What is an Emergency Work (EWOP) notice with the NYC Department of Buildings?
faqs.answer: An EWOP permits licensed general contractors to perform immediate structural stabilization and make-safe repairs to eliminate acute safety hazards before formal architectural work permits are issued.

faqs.question: Do you bill directly to commercial or residential property insurance carriers?
faqs.answer: Yes. We document all structural damage with date-stamped thermal infrared photos, atmospheric moisture logs, and itemized Xactimate estimates to streamline direct insurance claims.

faqs.question: How do you secure retail storefronts or residential buildings after a fire or vehicle impact?
faqs.answer: We deploy heavy-duty 3/4-inch CDX plywood security barriers anchored with steel carriage bolts, structural shoring posts, and install tamper-resistant keyless security access doors.

faqs.question: Can you stop severe active roof leaks during a major rainstorm?
faqs.answer: Yes. Our storm crews deploy temporary weighted ballast tarps, cold-applied emergency elastomeric mastic, and commercial diverter catch basins to arrest interior flooding immediately.

faqs.question: What should property owners do immediately after firefighters clear an emergency scene?
faqs.answer: Property owners should contact an emergency general contractor immediately to secure the building against weather intrusion, unauthorized entry, and structural collapse. Once fire officials declare the building safe to approach, securing exterior breaches with sturdy board-up panels and tarping exposed roof sections prevents further property loss. Mega Contracting NY Group dispatches emergency crews to stabilize structural members, isolate utility connections, and secure your property from outside elements while planning stabilization, temporary power, and cleanup.

faqs.question: How does water from firefighting efforts complicate fire damage recovery?
faqs.answer: Standing water saturates building materials, weakens plaster and subfloors, and causes mold growth if not extracted within twenty-four to forty-eight hours. The thousands of gallons of water used to extinguish building fires pool in wall cavities, seep across finished flooring, and soak structural framing. Our emergency response team deploys high-volume water extractors, industrial air movers, and dehumidifiers immediately to dry the structure before fungal contamination sets in and degrades structural wood or causes persistent mildew odors.

faqs.question: What is an Emergency Work Notice with the city building department?
faqs.answer: An Emergency Work Notice is an administrative filing that notifies municipal building authorities that urgent stabilization work is being performed to address acute safety hazards. In emergency scenarios involving partial collapses, fire damage, or vehicle impacts, licensed general contractors can execute immediate make-safe shoring and protective enclosures before standard architectural permits are issued. We handle emergency filings directly, ensuring urgent stabilization satisfies municipal safety mandates and avoids administrative penalties.

faqs.question: Why is professional soot and smoke residue removal necessary?
faqs.answer: Soot contains corrosive acidic compounds that etch glass, pit metals, and deeply permeate porous masonry and structural timber if left untreated. Wiping soot with household cleaners often smears the oily residue deeper into wall surfaces, causing permanent staining and persistent smoke odors. Our crews use specialized dry chemical sponges, thermal fogging, and HEPA-filtered vacuuming equipment to lift acidic soot particles from structural surfaces without causing further damage to underlying materials. We also deploy industrial hydroxyl generators and air scrubbers to neutralize volatile airborne aromatic molecules throughout building cavities.

faqs.question: Can building occupants enter a fire-damaged building to retrieve personal belongings?
faqs.answer: Occupants should not enter a damaged building until municipal authorities and licensed structural contractors confirm the premises are structurally sound. Burned floor joists, weakened stairwells, and hanging ceiling plaster present severe safety hazards to untrained individuals. Once emergency shoring and perimeter stabilization are completed by our team, property owners can safely coordinate the retrieval of essential personal documents and valuables under supervision while wearing proper protective gear, helmets, and respirators.

faqs.question: How do you coordinate with insurance adjusters during emergency restoration?
faqs.answer: We document all visible damage through extensive photo catalogs, thermal moisture imaging, and itemized structural stabilization summaries for your insurance claim. When adjusters arrive to inspect the property, having detailed initial condition records and clear physical scopes of work accelerates claim processing. We provide adjusters with itemized documentation of emergency shoring, board-up materials, and extraction labor to support a smooth claim settlement without procedural delays. Our coordinators maintain detailed daily equipment and labor distribution logs across all affected property sectors.
